headline: BlackRock chief executive Larry Fink warned that the United States would fall into recession if a halt on data centre building were put in place.
score_reason: Facts match the headline for the Fink half; the Morgan Stanley half is only in the SBS headline.
importance_line: Workers in construction and the power trades and US households that depend on growth are affected first, then utilities and data centre builders; Fink's warning comes from the head of a firm with large investments in the sector and is not a consensus forecast.
summary: Yahoo Finance reports that Larry Fink, chief executive of BlackRock, the world's largest asset manager, told CNBC on 14 Oct 2026 that 'if we have a moratorium of some sort in this country, we will be in a recession', and notes that this is his warning rather than a consensus forecast. SBS News carried the story the same day under a headline that adds that Morgan Stanley vowed to keep investing in AI.
notes: The listed SBS News page only showed its headline and a short lede (HTTP 200, 670 characters); the Fink detail was read in the Yahoo Finance article about the same CNBC interview. The Morgan Stanley half of the SBS headline could not be checked and is not detailed. Source set to Yahoo Finance, where the text was read.
